skill.name: helm-chart-scaffolding
skill.description: Create and validate Helm chart scaffolds for Kubernetes applications, including Chart.yaml metadata, values files, templates, dependencies, and multi-environment patterns.
skill.summary: Scaffold reusable Helm charts and validation workflows for Kubernetes applications.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged many URLs, shell snippets, filesystem redirects, and environment-value examples. Context review shows those detections are Helm documentation, reusable templates, or a local validation script rather than malicious behavior. One semantic issue remains: the examples include a weak default PostgreSQL password that should not be deployable as-is.

remediation.issue: Default PostgreSQL password is set to changeme in chart examples.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the value with an empty placeholder and require existingSecret or external secret management for database credentials.

remediation.issue: Environment variable examples could be mistaken for a place to store secrets.
remediation.suggestion: State that .Values.env is only for non-sensitive settings and route secrets through Kubernetes Secret references.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Default Database Password
semantic_findings.description: The chart values template and guide set PostgreSQL auth.password to "changeme". A scaffold copied into production could deploy a predictable database password.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The weak password is explicitly shown as a default value in reusable chart examples. It is a common deployable default credential risk if users copy the scaffold unchanged.

content.value_statement: Helm charts are hard to structure consistently across environments. This skill provides chart layouts, values patterns, and validation steps for Kubernetes releases.
actual_capabilities: Defines standard Helm chart directory structures and required files.
Provides Chart.yaml and values.yaml templates for common Kubernetes applications.
Shows reusable Helm template helpers, labels, and naming conventions.
Explains dependency management for subcharts such as PostgreSQL and Redis.
Includes validation commands and a local chart validation script.
Covers multi-environment values files, hooks, tests, and repository packaging.
limitations: Does not generate application-specific Kubernetes manifests without user requirements.
Does not validate charts against a live cluster by itself.
Requires Helm and optional tools such as jq for the validation script.
Example dependency versions and repositories may need updates before production use.

use_cases.title: Create a New Service Chart
use_cases.description: Scaffold a Helm chart for a web service with values, templates, dependencies, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Standardize Release Configuration
use_cases.description: Organize environment-specific values files for development, staging, and production releases.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Chart for Distribution
use_cases.description: Package a chart, create a repository index, and document expected installation and test workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic Helm chart scaffold for a Kubernetes web service named my-app. Include the required files and explain each file briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Design Values Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a values.yaml structure for a stateless API service. Include image, service, ingress, resources, probes, autoscaling, and security context settings.

prompt_templates.title: Add Dependencies and Environments
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend an existing Helm chart with optional PostgreSQL and Redis dependencies. Add separate values for development, staging, and production.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Production Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Helm chart design for production readiness. Check templates, helper functions, values schema, dependencies, hooks, tests, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Request a Helm chart scaffold for a new API service.
output_examples.output: A chart plan with required files, recommended templates, default values, helper functions, and validation commands.

output_examples.input: Ask for production and staging values organization.
output_examples.output: A clear environment strategy with shared defaults, override files, resource settings, ingress choices, and dependency toggles.

output_examples.input: Ask how to validate a chart before release.
output_examples.output: A validation checklist covering linting, template rendering, dry runs, dependencies, schema checks, probes, and security settings.

best_practices: Pin chart dependency versions and keep Chart.lock updated.
Document every values.yaml field and validate important values with a schema.
Keep secrets out of plain values files and prefer external secret management.
anti_patterns: Using one large chart for unrelated applications.
Embedding production secrets or passwords directly in values.yaml.
Skipping linting, template rendering, and dry-run checks before release.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete Helm chart?
faq.answer: It provides scaffold patterns, templates, and validation steps. Application-specific manifests still need user requirements.

faq.question: Can I use this with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it support Helm 3 charts?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use Chart.yaml apiVersion v2, which is used by Helm 3.

faq.question: Does it include chart validation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes linting, template rendering, dry-run installation, dependency checks, and optional schema validation.

faq.question: Does it manage secrets securely?
faq.answer: It mentions external secret management, but users must avoid storing real secrets in plain values files.

faq.question: Can it help with multi-environment releases?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to organize development, staging, and production values files.
